task: Track 2 — example test data (specific military goods, NOT war materiel) for POST /advise classification
notes: Precedence: KMV Annex 1 (war materiel list, KM 1-22) always prevails. An item that is war materiel is NOT a specific military good under GKV Annex 3.
Every item in this file is a specific military good under GKV Annex 3 that has NO counterpart in KMV Annex 1, so the expected regime is `specific_military`.
Why each group is not war materiel:
- ML 14, 15, 18 and 22 have no counterpart: KM 14, 15, 18 and 22 are empty ('Enthält kein KM').

- ML 7 biological/chemical agents: KM 7 lists ONLY the four riot-control agents (CA, CS, CN, CR). Chemical warfare agents, biological agents and CBRN protective/detection equipment are NOT war materiel — note CS/CN/CR ARE war materiel under KM 7.

- ML 8 oxidizers, binders and additives: KM 8 covers only explosives/propellants/pyrotechnics meeting its performance parameters (or military pyrotechnics / specially designed military aircraft fuels); simple chemical materials without such parameters are not war materiel.
- ML 16: KM 16 covers only forgings/castings for KM 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 10, 12 or 19 goods; a forging for an ML-14 good is therefore ML 16.

- ML 21: KM 21 covers only software for goods ON the KM list; software for ML-only goods (ML 14, ML 15, ML 17) is ML 21. (Contrast: fire-control software for a KM 5 weapon system is KM 21 war materiel.)

- ML 17: KM 17 covers only robots, parametric libraries and nuclear power plants for combat; diving apparatus is ML 17. Contrast: an armoured mobile crane truck particularly designed for military purposes is a land vehicle under KM 6 war materiel, not ML 17.

Contrast with ML 11: electronic equipment 'particularly designed for combat' (incl. ECM/ECCM and underwater countermeasures) IS war materiel under KM 11 — do not classify such items as specific_military.
Each entry's `request` is a ready-to-send /advise payload (item block only).
`expected` is the ground truth for scoring: controlled flag, regime, control list entries.
specifications are deliberately free-form (varied keys/units), matching the API contract.
